why: Removing C3 eliminated the short-complement binding that had discouraged cuts near verbs, so the model began placing more cuts earlier/around predicates; that produced modest gains for longer-latency pieces (by_bin shows the biggest positive change in the ≤99 and mid-length bins) but also increased harmful subject–verb splits and fragmented enumerations in short/medium bins, leaving the overall H_set change near zero.
lesson: If you remove the short-complement binding, you must preserve a constraint that prevents cutting immediately between subjects and their verbs and that avoids splitting list items, because deletion alone trades away those short-bin harms for only modest long-bin gains.
